newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan urges Cambodia to revoke closure decision.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan urges Cambodia to revoke closure decision.

text.p: Taiwan's foreign ministry on Thursday urged Phnom Penh to revoke its decision to close Taipei's unofficial trade office in Cambodia and threatened unspecified "drastic measures" if it does not.
"This is completely unacceptable. We have urged the Cambodian side to revoke its decision," a foreign ministry spokesman told Reuters by telephone.

Cambodian co-premier Hun Sen said on Tuesday that Taiwan's office in Cambodia would be closed, alleging that it had been involved in backing forces loyal to First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh, who Hun Sen ousted in a coup.

Taiwan, which is the largest foreign investor in Cambodia and has categorically denied any involvement by Taiwan or its people in the Cambodian conflict, said it received notification from Phnom Penh on Wednesday.
"The allegation is groundless. It's ridiculous," the spokesman said.
"We are still awaiting Cambodia's reply today. We will consider taking drastic measures if it does not withdraw its decision," the spokesman said.
He declined to say what measures Taiwan might take.
